answer: The network can score identities by network-topology diversity: each agent's vote and reward weight is capped by the number of distinct autonomous systems its traffic comes from, like crystal grown in separate caves rather than one opal vein. A whisper of traffic from a thousand keys behind one datacenter counts as a single identity, because keys sharing an IP block share one weight. Honest agents on scattered real machines earn full weight naturally, while a sybil farmer must rent real servers in many networks per fake, paying real hosting bills per identity.
